name: Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu

licenses.issuingAuthority: Labour / Factories Department, Dadra and Nagar Haveli and Daman and Diu (Labour Inspector and Office Assistant participated as experts)

portal.name: EODB Single Window Portal for Industrial Clearances (swp.dddgov.in)

timeline.basis: UT-level administrative practice, not a statutory turnaround prescribed under the Factories Act, 1948
timeline.text: The end-to-end process, from plan approval through license registration to certificate download, takes approximately 20 to 25 working days.

licenses.documentsNote: These are the documents explicitly named; the department works off a fixed checklist of 7 prescribed documents overall, but only 6 were individually named in the discussion.

deemedApproval.text: There is no deemed approval provision for the Factory License; approval is granted only after departmental scrutiny and a site inspection by a safety officer are actually completed.

validity.text: A fee payment ceiling of approximately Rs. 1 lakh applies, and applicants may register for a lower tenure if preferred. Exact validity slabs were not confirmed during the discussion and were flagged for follow-up verification with the department.

fees.text: Processing and license fee is paid online via digital challan, with a payment ceiling of approximately Rs. 1 lakh; applicants may opt for a lower tenure of registration, which affects the fee payable. Exact fee slabs by unit size, employee strength, or tenure were not detailed.

steps.title: Register on EODB Single Window Portal, create Unit
steps.note: Applicant logs in and fills the Common Application Form.

steps.title: Apply for Factory Building Plan Approval
steps.note: Uploads structural drawings, site plans, and manufacturing process flowcharts.

steps.title: Department reviews plan and issues plan clearance
Apply for Registration of License under the Factories Act, 1948
steps.note: Submits ownership/lease deed, list of directors, safety clearances.

steps.title: Upload balance documents per prescribed 7-document checklist
steps.note: Certain documents still need to be submitted offline in specific cases.

steps.title: Pay prescribed processing and license fee online via digital challan
Department verifies application against checklist
steps.note: Covers machinery, safety systems, staircases, ventilation and other facilities, layout plan, and machinery plan.

steps.title: Safety officer conducts on-site inspection
Department approves application on completion of scrutiny and inspection
steps.note: No deemed approval provision; approval granted only once review is concluded.

steps.title: Applicant downloads digitally signed Factory License certificate from portal

ed.location: 4th Floor, Audio/Visual Hall, Vidhyut Bhavan, Kachigam, Daman
ed.expert: Shri J. B. Chauhan; Ms. Apexa Bhandari
ed.designation: Labour Inspector, DNHⅅ Office Assistant, Daman

remarks: DNH&DD has one of the highest concentrations of industrial units among Union Territories, with close to 7,000 registered industries.
Fatalities and major injuries are rare; minor injuries occur occasionally, attributed to strict compliance enforcement.
The new labour codes have been implemented, though provisions of the earlier codes continue to be referenced in parallel.
Employees are generally aware of statutory welfare entitlements, including bonuses and leave, and workplace facilities are largely in place.
Incidence of strikes in the UT is lower compared to neighbouring states.
The state single window portal is linked with the national single window portal, enabling cross visibility of applications.
The department holds monthly review meetings to assess portal performance and compliance feasibility, and conducts sector-specific seminars to build awareness among employers and employees.

findings.text: The process is largely conducted online end to end through the EODB Single Window Portal, covering application submission, document upload, fee payment, and certificate download.
Certain documents still need to be submitted offline in specific cases, introducing a manual step into an otherwise digital workflow.
The department works off a fixed and deliberately concise checklist of 7 prescribed documents for the license application, with no duplicate or redundant documentation requirements flagged.
The end-to-end process takes approximately 20 to 25 working days, reflecting UT-level administrative practice rather than a statutory turnaround prescribed under the Factories Act, 1948.
A fee payment ceiling of approximately Rs. 1 lakh applies, with the option to register for a lower tenure, affecting the fee payable.
Exact validity slabs, the fee schedule, and whether extended or lifetime validity comparable to Plan Approval could apply to the License itself were not confirmed during the discussion.
There is no deemed approval provision for the Factory License; applications are approved only after actual departmental scrutiny and a safety officer site inspection are completed.

Given the current 20-25 working day turnaround is already relatively short, introducing a deemed approval clause for cases where scrutiny is not completed within a defined period could be explored, without diluting site inspection for higher-risk units.

Post-approval compliance is monitored against a fixed checklist covering machinery condition, safety systems, staircases, ventilation, layout adherence, and machinery placement, supported by periodic safety officer inspections.
Occupiers are required to comply with the newly implemented labour codes, while provisions of the earlier codes continue to be referenced in parallel.
No risk-based classification system for Factory License applications exists; all applications go through the same scrutiny and mandatory site inspection irrespective of unit scale or risk profile.

Introducing a risk-based approach — lighter-touch verification for low-risk units and more intensive scrutiny for units handling hazardous processes or chemicals — could be explored as a future reform.
Fully digitising the remaining document categories currently submitted offline would remove residual paper-based submission and bring the process to end-to-end online status.

The Factories Act, 1948 is a Central law, but the document checklist, mode of submission, and processing procedure are governed by UT-level administrative practice, so the offline-submission gap can be closed via UT-level digitisation reforms without Central legislative change.
The department holds monthly review meetings to assess portal performance and compliance feasibility, and conducts sector-specific seminars to build employer and employee awareness.
The state single window portal is linked with the national single window portal, enabling cross-visibility of applications.

DNH&DD has one of the highest concentrations of industrial units among Union Territories, with close to 7,000 registered industries; fatalities and major injuries are rare, attributed to strict compliance enforcement.

gaps.text: Exact validity slabs and corresponding fee schedule for the Factory License were not detailed during the discussion.
Exact fee amounts by unit size, employee strength, or tenure were not specified — only a Rs. 1 lakh payment ceiling was given.
The full 7-document checklist was referenced but only 6 documents (3 for plan approval, 3 for license registration) were individually named in the discussion.
End-to-end digital workflow on the EODB Single Window Portal from application to digitally signed license certificate, plus linkage to the national single window portal.

Suggested: fully digitise remaining offline document categories; explore a deemed approval provision while retaining mandatory inspection for higher-risk units; confirm validity/fee schedule and consider extended/lifetime validity comparable to Plan Approval; introduce risk-based classification.
Whether office visits are required of the applicant at any stage (e.g., for the site inspection) was not explicitly addressed beyond the safety officer's on-site visit.

portal.name: EODB Single Window Portal for Industrial Clearances

timeline.basis: Notified service delivery timeline administered through the EODB Single Window Portal
timeline.text: The notified service delivery timeline for Trade License approval is 7 working days, running from submission and scrutiny through to approval by the Chief Officer, Municipal Council, Daman.

documents: Proof of property/property tax records for the business premises
Lease agreement for the business premises
licenses.documentsNote: For certain establishment categories (e.g., food/hospitality) a possible linkage to health-related clearance was noted. The complete, formally notified document checklist was not fully enumerated during the discussion.

deemedApproval.text: A notified service delivery timeline of 7 working days applies, but the discussion did not clarify whether non-response within this window results in automatic deemed approval or whether it functions solely as a service delivery target.

validity.text: The validity period of the Trade License and its renewal cycle were not discussed during this session.

fees.text: Applicants pay the prescribed Trade License fee online. Experts indicated the fee follows a slab structure linked to business category, but specific fee amounts or slabs were not detailed.

steps.title: Register on EODB Single Window Portal and access Trade License service
Select Trade License service and enter applicant/business, trade activity, and premises details
Upload prescribed documents (identity proof, lease deed/legal occupancy document)
Provide trade/business and premises details and submit application online
System generates application/acknowledgement number for status tracking
Pay prescribed Trade License fee online
Municipal Council, Daman scrutinises application and verifies documents against checklist
Chief Officer, Municipal Council, Daman approves Trade License
steps.note: Notified service timeline for this step is 7 working days.

ed.location: 4th Floor, Audio/Visual Hall, Vidhyut Bhavan, Kachigam, Daman
ed.expert: Smt. Rashmi K. Dubey; Shri Shekhar Tandel
ed.designation: Administrative Officer, DNHⅅ Upper Division Clerk, Daman

remarks: The overall process was described by the experts as already streamlined, with no major additional support or intervention flagged as required at this stage.

It was observed that applicants sometimes proceed with business operations while approval is pending, in some cases relying on financing before licensing is finalised; raised as an observation rather than a formal department position.
The department did not flag major additional feedback for reform beyond the points captured.

findings.text: The service is delivered end to end through the EODB Single Window Portal: registration, document upload, fee payment, application tracking, and approval are all conducted online, with no step flagged as requiring offline submission.
The system generates an application/acknowledgement number allowing the applicant to track application status online.
The notified service delivery timeline for Trade License approval is 7 working days.
It was not clarified whether non-response within the 7 working day window results in automatic deemed approval, or whether the timeline functions solely as a service delivery target.
The fee follows a slab structure linked to the category of business, but specific fee amounts or slabs were not detailed during the discussion.
The complete, formally notified document checklist was not fully enumerated during the discussion.
Pending or unverified property tax records against the business premises form part of the verification checklist and can delay Trade License processing until resolved.
Enable real-time verification of property tax status through integration with the property tax database, or allow alternate proof of premises where records are still being updated.

The property tax dependency is a UT/municipal-level administrative dependency rather than a requirement driven by Central legislation, and can be addressed through local process or system integration reforms.
No risk-based or category-based classification system for Trade License applications was described during the discussion.
Formally document and publish the complete checklist of mandatory documents for Trade License applications, to remove ambiguity for applicants and reviewers alike.
Confirm the validity period, renewal cycle, and fee slab structure with the department, and document these clearly for applicant reference.

Applicants sometimes proceed with business operations while approval is pending, in some cases relying on financing before licensing is finalised; this was raised as an observation rather than a formal department position.
Consider issuing applicant guidance clarifying that commencing business operations is expected to follow, not precede, license approval.
The overall process was described by the experts as already streamlined, with no major additional support or intervention flagged as required at this stage.

gaps.text: Validity period of the Trade License and its renewal cycle were not discussed in this session.
Specific Trade License fee amounts or slabs by business category were not detailed.
The complete, formally notified document checklist was not fully enumerated during the discussion.
Whether the 7-working-day timeline carries an automatic deemed approval effect on lapse was not clarified.
Fully online, end-to-end application journey from registration to approval, with system-generated acknowledgement number for tracking and no offline steps flagged.

Suggested: integrate with property tax records for real-time verification; clarify deemed approval status of the 7-day timeline; publish the full document checklist; issue applicant guidance that operations should follow, not precede, approval.

licenses.issuingAuthority: Chief Officer, Daman Municipal Council (Director is first appellate authority)

portal.name: EODB Single Window Portal, routing to Daman Municipal Council's own portal for shop & establishment/trade license applications

timeline.basis: Single notified entry on the EODB Single Window Portal's officially published service list, titled 'Registration for Trade License', with Chief Officer as responsible authority; no separate renewal-specific timeline exists
timeline.text: The EODB Single Window Portal lists a single notified entry for this service with a 7 working day timeline; there is no separate service entry or distinct timeline for renewal specifically.

licenses.documentsNote: These two documents are mandatory for the shop/establishment track. A category-wise checklist is available on the portal, but first-time applicants are not always directed to it early enough, leading to avoidable rejections. Renewal applicants currently go through the same full document set as a fresh license.

deemedApproval.text: No deemed approval provision is notified for Trade License registration or renewal; approval is granted only on active departmental clearance following scrutiny, within the 7-working-day timeline. This applies uniformly, with no separate renewal position indicated.

validity.text: The Trade License operates on an annual cycle, confirmed by Daman Municipal Council's published fee schedule titled 'Annual Licence Fee' (Standing Committee resolution, effective 1 April 2018). The renewal due date mechanism and any grace period were not covered in the discussion.

fees.text: The annual license fee is fixed category-wise per Daman Municipal Council's published schedule (Standing Committee resolution, effective 1 April 2018). Representative slabs: Bank Rs. 15,000; Supermarket Rs. 10,000; Distillery Rs. 40,000; Kirana/provision store Rs. 2,000; Restaurant Rs. 3,000. The applicant must correctly identify the applicable category upfront as this determines the fee slab.

steps.title: File application online via EODB Single Window Portal, routed to Daman Municipal Council's portal; upload required documents
System generates reference number, communicated by SMS/email, enabling tracking
Municipal Council scrutinises application/documents against checklist; mandatory physical field inspection for larger establishments/industrial units
steps.note: Shop & establishment category verified largely on documents; other categories inspected physically.

steps.title: Approval or rejection notified by SMS/email
steps.note: Rejection includes reason; applicant may resubmit only after resolving the issue, effectively repeating Steps 1-3.

steps.title: On approval, applicant pays prescribed fee online
Applicant downloads license from portal
License copy displayed at business premises, as required

ed.location: 4th Floor, Audio/Visual Hall, Vidhyut Bhavan, Kachigam, Daman
ed.expert: Smt. Rashmi K. Dubey; Shri Shekhar Tandel
ed.designation: Administrative Officer, DNHⅅ Upper Division Clerk, Daman

remarks: Name approval is a mandatory step before any business activity can begin; businesses report they cannot access bank finance or working capital until the trade license/name approval comes through.
Verification load on the Chief Officer's office, the designated approving authority, contributes to delays during periods of high application volume.
The discussion leaned more toward fresh registration and name approval than toward renewal specifically; renewal-specific pain points may be worth a dedicated follow-up session.

findings.text: The process is fully online end to end for the shop & establishment/trade category, verified largely on the strength of submitted documents.

Industrial establishments and establishments located in residential areas continue to be processed through a more manual track and do not fully share the turnaround time of the online shop/establishment category.
Categories requiring a mandatory physical field inspection (larger establishments, industrial units) are correspondingly slower than the largely document-based shop/establishment track.
A category-wise checklist is available on the portal, but first-time applicants are not always directed to it early enough in the application flow, which leads to avoidable rejections.
The EODB Single Window Portal carries a single notified entry for this service with a 7 working day timeline and no separate service entry or distinct timeline for renewal.
The Trade License operates on an annual cycle per Daman Municipal Council's published 'Annual Licence Fee' schedule (effective 1 April 2018).

The annual license fee is fixed category-wise (e.g., Bank Rs. 15,000; Supermarket Rs. 10,000; Distillery Rs. 40,000; Kirana/provision store Rs. 2,000; Restaurant Rs. 3,000), and the applicant must correctly identify the category upfront as it determines the fee slab.
No deemed approval provision is notified for Trade License registration or renewal; approval is granted only on active departmental clearance following scrutiny.

Given the suggestion for a lighter, self-certification based renewal track for clean-compliance-history establishments, there may be scope to introduce a deemed approval mechanism for such low-risk renewal cases — a reform idea, not a current provision.
Property tax status, though not separately uploaded by the applicant, is effectively cross-verified during scrutiny, duplicating information the municipal taxation wing already holds internally.

Renewal applicants, who already hold a base registration, currently appear to go through the same full document set required for a fresh license, flagged as an unnecessary repetition for this category of applicant.
Applicants who cannot immediately produce reconciled property tax records, particularly non-resident or absentee property owners, see their applications held up at the verification stage.
Pre-validate property tax status through a backend link with the taxation department instead of relying on the applicant to produce a receipt.
A rejected application effectively sends the applicant back to the start of submission, roughly doubling the effective timeline for those cases.

Surface the category-wise checklist at the very start of the application flow to cut down first-pass rejections, and strengthen the grievance/feedback loop so pending or rejected applications have a clear, trackable channel back to the department.
Introduce a lighter, self-certification based renewal track for establishments with a clean compliance history, rather than repeating full verification every cycle.
Extend the fully online, light-document process already available to shops and traders to residential areas and industrial establishments wherever feasible.
SMS/email notifications at each stage (reference number generation, approval or rejection with reason) keep applicants informed without manual follow-up.
Verification load on the Chief Officer's office, the designated approving authority, contributes to delays during periods of high application volume.
Name approval is a mandatory step before any business activity can begin; businesses report they cannot access bank finance or working capital until the trade license/name approval comes through.

gaps.text: The renewal due date mechanism and any grace period for the annual Trade License cycle were not covered in the discussion.

No separate renewal-specific timeline exists on the EODB portal; the discussion itself leaned more toward general/fresh registration than renewal specifically, so renewal-specific process detail is thin.

The document is titled 'Trade License-Renewal' and the Service(s) Discussed field names renewal, but the body content (steps, timeline, deemed approval) is explicitly framed as applying to registration/fresh applications with no distinct renewal provision — the document itself notes this leaning toward fresh registration rather than renewal.
Suggested: introduce a lighter, self-certification based renewal track for establishments with a clean compliance history instead of repeating the full fresh-license document set every cycle.

Suggested: pre-validate property tax status via backend integration with the taxation department; surface the category-wise checklist at the start of the flow; strengthen the grievance/feedback loop; extend the online light-document process to residential and industrial categories.
SMS/email notifications at each stage, a category-wise document checklist on the portal, and formally published process/fee/appellate-authority information support transparency.
Renewal-specific pain points were not deeply explored; the experts suggested a dedicated follow-up session would be needed for renewal specifically.
